false_alarm_details: Predicted a nit about 'reviewers may verify padding_idx is truly unused'. In reality no reviewer raised this concern — DarkLight1337 was already confident padding_idx was unused (he originally suggested the broader removal). The verification question was never a point of discussion.
key_insight: For simple mechanical deletions of dead code, reviewers don't ask for verification that the code is unused — especially when a core maintainer already confirmed it. The predicted nit was overly cautious; experienced maintainers know their codebase well enough to approve confidently without requesting explicit proof.
hypothesis: The false alarm came from projecting a generic 'careful reviewer' persona onto a codebase where maintainers have high familiarity. For trivially simple PRs (pure deletions of dead code), predicting zero substantive comments would have been more accurate. The lesson: when confidence is very high on a mechanical change, don't manufacture a hedging nit just to have a predicted comment — predict silence instead.
